meta.title: Strategy deck (about 6 slides) for a mid-size Indian agri-inputs company deciding whether to enter the drone-spraying services market. Must include: a

slides.title: A phased partner-led entry into drone-spraying services gives the company the fastest path to scale with controlled investment
slides.subtitle: Strategy deck for a mid-size Indian agri-inputs company assessing entry into the drone-spraying services market

slides.title: Drone-spraying services fit the company’s existing channel, advisory model, and farmer relationships closely enough to support a credible adjacent business
slides.subtitle: The fit is strongest where current assets already match service delivery needs, letting the company extend from product sales into recurring acreage-based execution.

principles.text: Existing **dealer reach** already provides local farmer access, lead generation, and issue resolution for a service sale.
Current **crop advisory** capabilities translate directly into spray-planning, dosage guidance, and season-based service triggers.
Farmer relationships built through input sales support trust in outsourced field operations and repeat bookings across seasons.
A partner-led operating model lets the company add drone capacity without building a full in-house fleet on day one.

slides.table_heading: Current assets map directly to the capabilities required to sell and deliver drone-spraying services

groups.label: Commercial fit
rows: Prioritise crops with repeat spray windows

groups.label: Delivery fit
rows: Use company protocols in partner operations
Build recurring acreage accounts before expansion

groups.label: Economic fit
rows: Avoids full fleet ownership at launch
Phase capex after demand is proven
Roll out in clusters, not nationwide at once

goals: The company has a credible right to win because service demand can be sourced through the same farmer access points used today
The operating model fits a phased launch because delivery capability can be added through partners while commercial ownership stays in-house
The adjacency is stronger than a cold-start service entry because advisory, relationships, and channel assets already exist

slides.title: Channel-led partnerships and pilot clusters should lead entry because they pair **high strategic fit** with **easier execution**
slides.subtitle: Illustrative 2x2 prioritisation of entry moves: start with the top-right plays, sequence lower-fit or harder-to-execute moves later.

blocks.title: Channel-led partnerships sit in the priority zone
blocks.body: Position: **high strategic fit**, **easier execution**. Uses the existing distributor base, input-led farmer access, and field activation model.

blocks.title: Pilot clusters convert early demand into repeatable delivery
blocks.body: Position: **high strategic fit**, **easier execution**. Concentrates demand, operator supply, training, and proof points in a tight geography.

blocks.title: Company-owned fleet build-out is harder to execute at entry
blocks.body: Position: **high strategic fit**, **harder execution**. Requires upfront fleet, operations control, maintenance processes, and local capacity before demand is proven.

blocks.title: Standalone digital marketplace models should follow, not lead
blocks.body: Position: **low strategic fit**, **harder execution**. Relies less on the core channel and advisory strengths while needing rapid two-sided network build.

slides.title: A partner-led model reaches farmers fastest while avoiding the operating load of a fully owned fleet and the control gaps of a pure marketplace
slides.subtitle: Illustrative comparison of three entry models for drone-spraying services

cells.text: Launches through **25** channel partners across **8** districts with a central team of **12** people.
Company controls farmer sourcing, pricing guardrails, SOPs, and product linkage while partners operate **60** drones.
Requires hiring **85** field and ops staff and standing up maintenance, pilot scheduling, compliance, and spares management in **8** districts.
Highest control over service quality and data capture, but the fleet starts with only **45%** utilisation.
Fastest to launch with **80** listed operators across **10** districts and a lean team of **6** people.
Lowest control on service quality, pricing discipline, and product pull-through; only **35%** of jobs use linked input bundles.

summary_band.label: WHY PARTNER-LED WINS
segments: **3 months** to launch vs **9 months** for a fully owned fleet
**₹1 crore** capex keeps entry light vs **₹9 crore** for full ownership
**28%** gross margin is materially stronger than the marketplace at **12%**
Control stays high enough to link service delivery with input sales across **25** partners and **60** drones

slides.title: A **12-month** rollout from pilot districts to scaled clusters lets the company validate unit economics before expanding fleet capacity and coverage
slides.subtitle: Illustrative phased path from initial pilots to scaled operating clusters, with each step tied to proof points before the next capacity build

phases.title: Pilot design locks target crops, districts, partner terms, and service SOPs before field launch
phases.body: Define pilot scope for **2** districts, **3** crops, and **1** operating playbook; set commercial terms, lead routing, and spray-quality checks.

phases.title: District pilots test demand conversion and delivery reliability before broader capacity commitments
phases.body: Run pilots with **4** partners and **8** drones; track leads, booked demos, quoted acreage, completed jobs, and repeat demand by district.

phases.title: A mid-year economics gate determines whether expansion follows proven contribution margins and utilisation
phases.body: At **Month 6**, review pilot metrics against **3** thresholds: partner productivity, drone utilisation, and signed acreage conversion.

phases.title: Scaled clusters expand coverage only after the model works, adding capacity in sequenced waves
phases.body: Expand to **6** clusters with **12** partners and **24** drones by **Month 12**, then widen district coverage through the same partner-led playbook.

slides.title: Tight conversion management can turn **1,000** leads into **12,000 acres** of signed demand across the booking funnel
slides.subtitle: Illustrative funnel of the drone-spraying service pipeline, showing how disciplined qualification, quoting, and booking translate outreach into contracted acreage.

chart.annotation: The pipeline narrows from 1,000 leads to 80 bookings and ends at 12,000 acres of signed demand.

insights.text: **1,000** leads narrow to **400** qualified farmers, concentrating effort on serviceable demand.
The middle funnel converts **220** field surveys into **160** quotes, keeping pre-sales activity tied to real booking intent.
**80** bookings produce **12,000 acres** of signed demand, making booked acreage the output that matters.

slides.title: Launching now through phased partnerships converts strategic fit into scalable acreage with faster validation and lower operating load

sections.heading: Why now
sections.body: The company already has the ingredients to start: existing channel access, advisory relationships, and farmer trust support a credible adjacent service without building a fully owned fleet first.

sections.heading: How to enter
sections.body: Lead with channel-led partnerships and pilot clusters. This route combines **high strategic fit** with **easier execution**, reaches farmers fastest, and avoids the operating load of a fully owned fleet and the control gaps of a pure marketplace.

sections.heading: What the first year proves
sections.body: A **12-month** rollout from pilot districts to scaled clusters validates unit economics before adding fleet capacity and geographic coverage, turning early pilots into a repeatable expansion model.

sections.heading: What scales
sections.body: Disciplined conversion management translates commercial activity into booked demand: **1,000** leads progress through the funnel to **12,000 acres** of signed demand, giving the business a measurable path from pipeline to scale.
